chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife before consummating the marriage, is there a waiting period (iddah) for her? He said, 'No.' I said to him, [What about] the one whose husband dies before consummating the marriage, is there a waiting period for her? He said, 'Hold back from this.'

So these two narrations do not contradict the narrations we have presented earlier, because the latter narration does not explicitly state that he said 'there is no waiting period for her,' but rather he said 'hold back from this,' and it is not impossible that he (peace be upon him) said that for some reason of expediency he perceived in the situation.

And if it had contained an explicit statement that 'there is no waiting period for her' like the first narration, then it would not have been permissible to deviate from the preceding narrations, which agree with the apparent meaning of the Quran, to these two later anomalous narrations, because the ruling of this one is that is not explicit is not valid for action.
And that which also indicates that there is a waiting period for her, in addition to what we have presented, is what he narrated:

key_terms.عِدَّةٌ: Waiting period (iddah) for a woman after divorce or death of husband

ai.seo_question: Does a woman have a waiting period if her husband dies before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) responds to a query about the waiting period (iddah) of a woman whose husband dies before consummation with the phrase 'Hold back from this' (amsik 'an hadha). The scholar clarifies that this is not an explicit denial of iddah, thereby preserving the general rule derived from the apparent meaning of the Quran, and notes that these reports do not contradict earlier established traditions.
